title: While with Counter
concept: Use a counter variable in a while loop to track iterations, accumulate values, or build results.
why: Counted loops are the most common loop pattern — processing N items, summing numbers, or building sequences.
tips: Initialize your counter BEFORE the loop
Update the counter INSIDE the loop body (usually at the end)
Check the condition carefully: `<` vs `<=` changes the number of iterations
Start counters at 0 (zero-indexed) or 1 (one-indexed) — be consistent
common_mistakes: Forgetting to update the counter — infinite loop!
Updating the counter at the wrong time — before or after using it matters
Off-by-one: running the loop one too many or one too few times
Using `let` instead of `var` for the counter — can't update a let
